externalFinding: The adopted 2026–2027 Economics track totals 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC courses in each of Years 1 and 2, 30 EC open study, three compulsory 6 EC final-year subjects and a 12 EC Economics thesis. Economics is the first-listed broad track in the official schedule, selected neutrally before UCR construction; Accounting, Finance and Marketing belong to the separate Business Economics track and are not mixed into this comparator. English teaching has Dutch tutorial, expression and exam-answer options in Years 1–2; Year 3 is English. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC and a pass in QRM I. The English diagnostic or completed refresher gates the Academic Skills grade. Zero-credit SAM provides mentor meetings each period, not added EC. The second-year Research Paper is a three-student project with data/model-based inquiry, paper, referee report and presentations; QRM I/II and Academic Skills are recommended background. Thesis entry at application requires 120 EC including QRM II, the entire first year, and at most two outstanding Year-2 courses. It is individual literature-review or empirical/theoretical economic research with thesis and video presentation; apply early October for periods 2–3 or late February for periods 5–6. These relative deadlines are not imposed as dated future-cohort deadlines. Open study normally requires 90 EC, at most 6 EC level 100, at least 12 EC level 300, no compulsory overlap and prior examination-board approval except SBE faculty, university or Education minors. Business Administration and Economics university minors are prohibited for EBE. Course manuals may require attendance; the Ethics tutorials and two online meetings are compulsory. Honours is additional. The main annual chart shows thesis12EC, but the specialisation subtable incorrectly prints6EC; the exact annual thesis catalogue independently confirms12EC. Retain12EC, not an invented extra unit or guessed two-part6EC allocation. Hidden duplicate text in the main chart is not an additional Macroeconomics course.
